findings.title: High-index bits survive the reset but are not permanent

evidence.fact: The contract says a set UPDATED bit above the quarter-reset extent stays true for process life/permanently after its first update.
The new header/reset-group commentary repeats lifetime persistence; the actual case only shows two resets and a read of that same bit.
All indices use the same word &= mask getter. Reading another entity in that word clears the first bit, including words outside the quarter-reset extent.

findings.impact: A future owner could incorrectly treat high-index UPDATED as immutable true or assume the supply descriptor must see its mask on every later iteration. The characterized cross-entity destructive read remains applicable above the reset boundary.
findings.minimum_correction: Replace permanence claims by survival of the reset and persistence only until a destructive neighbour read or another actual overwrite. Qualify the supply-descriptor explanation accordingly. Preserve the original &= behavior and recorded test results; no production repair, bool normalization or replay is required for a prose/comment correction.
